headline: Fed hike odds for next week fell to about 15%, and Bitcoin bounced to about $82.5K from last week's dip under $80K. Oil above $100 and 5% bond yields keep it boxed in.

stories.title: Fed hike odds fell to about 15%. So why is Bitcoin stuck near $82K?
stories.summary: After hot inflation data, traders priced about a 54% chance of a rate hike on 28 Oct. After Fed Chair Warsh spoke on 16 Oct, that fell to about 15–17%. Bitcoin bounced from near $79.8K, but oil and bond yields are capping it below about $84K.
points: September inflation (CPI) came in at 3.7% a year, above the 3.6% forecast.
Odds of a hike at the 28 Oct meeting: about 15–17% by most measures (CME FedWatch 16.1% at Friday's close). One source still says about 30%.
The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.33% after CPI and closed Friday near 5.1%. When safe bonds pay 5%, some money leaves crypto.
Oil is above $100 (WTI $101.35 Friday). Iran says mines hit tankers near Hormuz; that is not independently confirmed.
Last week's Bitcoin range: about $79.8K to $84.2K.

sources.label: Benzinga: Fed hike odds after Warsh remarks

stories.title: Charles Schwab now lets eligible clients buy Bitcoin and Ether
stories.summary: One of America's biggest brokers announced direct BTC and ETH trading on its Q3 earnings call. Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink are planned by year-end, according to one report.
points: Schwab holds more than $13 trillion of client assets.
One outlet reports a 0.75% fee per trade. Check Schwab's own fee page for the confirmed number.
Brokers and crypto exchanges differ on fees, coin choice, trading hours and whether you can withdraw coins to your own wallet.
Big brokers adding crypto is a sign of mainstream adoption. On its own, it doesn't move the price.

sources.label: Crypto Briefing: Schwab direct Bitcoin and Ether trading

stories.title: Strategy (MSTR) could be removed from MSCI indexes
stories.summary: MSCI finalised a rule on 15 Oct that can drop 'non-operating' companies such as Strategy and Metaplanet from its indexes. Funds that track those indexes would have to sell the stock.
points: The affected list comes out 11 Nov. Changes take effect at the close on 30 Nov.
JPMorgan earlier estimated about $2.8B of forced selling. That estimate came before the rule was final.
MSTR closed last week at $136.83, down 9.6%.
